proof.text: Write E=j_! and R=j^* for the underived module functors. Work on the small site representatives in [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison]; its exact equivalence identifies the relative tensors, the open adjunction and the actual lax tensor map with their ringed-topos counterparts. The coefficient comparison is invertible for every condensed ring by [lem-sfb-alpha-iso]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] makes R exact, and E is exact by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. The adjunction of [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction] lifts extension by zero and restriction: after the scalar identification alpha_j, its unit has underlying abelian-sheaf unit. That unit is invertible because the abelian extension by zero is fully faithful [sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek]: for an adjunction $F\dashv G$ with F fully faithful, lift $\varepsilon_{FM}$ to $v:GFM\to M$. Faithfulness and the first triangle identity give $v\eta_M=1$; naturality gives $\eta_Mv=G(Fv)\eta_{GFM}=G(\varepsilon_{FM})\eta_{GFM}=1$ by the other triangle identity. Its inverse is module-linear: if u is an invertible linear map, u^{-1}(a m)=a u^{-1}(m) follows by applying u. Hence the module unit is an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], E and R act termwise on representatives. The derived unit is the localization of this termwise unit (the comparison identifies the specified adjunction), so eta_K is an isomorphism for every K.

proof.text: First pass the abelian projection formula to relative tensor products. For module sheaves M on U and N on Z, use the symmetric form of [lem-sfb-open-projection-formula] to identify E(M tensor R N) with E M tensor N, with these tensors temporarily over $\mathbf Z$. The relative tensors are the coequalizers in [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. Under the abelian formula applied also with the extra coefficient-ring factor, the two arrows for the source coequalizer become exactly the two actions defining the target coequalizer: after alpha_j, both impose $(am)\otimes n=m\otimes(an)$. E preserves this coequalizer because it is a left adjoint [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek, lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Taking coequalizers of the isomorphic parallel-arrow diagrams gives an isomorphism theta_{M,N}:$E(M\otimes_{\Lambda_U}RN)\longrightarrow EM\otimes_{\Lambda_Z}N$. It is the canonical module mate: on the defining balanced bilinear map its transpose is (eta_M tensor 1) followed by the pullback tensor comparison. Thus the quotient construction proves invertibility of the specified map, not just of its endpoints.

proof.text: For complexes P on U and Q on Z, apply theta_{P^p,Q^q} in each bidegree. The functor E commutes with the direct sums in the total complex because it is a left adjoint [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek, lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. Hence these maps give an isomorphism E Tot(P tensor_{Lambda_U} R Q) -> Tot(E P tensor_{Lambda_Z} Q). With the convention of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], naturality in P^p makes theta commute with d_P tensor 1 and naturality in Q^q makes it commute with 1 tensor d_Q. Additivity preserves the scalar (-1)^p, so theta commutes with the sum d_P tensor 1+(-1)^p 1 tensor d_Q. Applying the inverse bidegree maps gives its chain inverse. This works for unbounded complexes because the total terms are direct sums, not products.

proof.text: Choose flat-term K-flat representatives P for K and Q for L using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], through the equivalence of Step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], R Q is K-flat with flat terms. The total complex E P is also K-flat: for any acyclic C on Z, R C is acyclic by exactness, P tensor R C is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex], and Step 3 identifies E(P tensor R C) with E P tensor C; exactness of E proves the latter acyclic. Each E(P^p) is flat as well: by Step 2, its tensor functor is E(P^p tensor R(-)), a composite of exact functors, so use [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. The equivalence of [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] preserves these notions, so these conclusions hold for the specified module-object tensors.

proof.text: Compute the displayed q on P,Q. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] and [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom], the total tensor complexes in Step 3 compute both derived tensor products, since P,R Q,E P,Q have the K-flat properties checked in Step 4. The unit and counit are the levelwise ones of Step 1. The canonical ringed-topos tensor comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; the precise transformation comparison in [lem-pd-module-ringed-topos-derived-comparison] identifies its inverse with the actual mu_j of the item. Consequently the representative of q is the direct-sum totalization of epsilon_{E(P^p) tensor Q^q} composed with E(mu_{E(P^p),Q^q}) composed with E(eta_{P^p} tensor 1). This is exactly theta in Step 2, by its adjoint-of-unit description. Step 3 supplies a chain inverse; localization therefore makes q_{j,K,L} invertible. All complexes in the statement admit the chosen resolutions, so this proves the ambient assertion without boundedness or constructibility.

proof.text: The formula for q is a composite of natural transformations (unit, tensor structure, counit), so it is natural in K,L independently of a choice of representatives. Under the adjunction, a map a -> r b corresponds to epsilon_b composed with e of that map. Apply this to a=K tensor r L and b=e K tensor L to obtain exactly the formula in the item. The symmetry exchanges K tensor r L with r L tensor K, and e K tensor L with L tensor e K. Naturality of the symmetry and the symmetric monoidal pullback comparison exchange eta tensor 1 with 1 tensor eta. The resulting adjoint is precisely the projection map in [def-sfb-adjunction-has-projection-formula].

These subcategories are full by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]; the ambient inverse to q is therefore a morphism of the full subcategory, and its two inverse identities remain true there. title: Canonical open projection formula for derived condensed module objects
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, and separated finite-type $k$-schemes as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], with coefficient ring objects $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$, put $e=D(j_!)$ for levelwise exact extension by zero of module objects [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek] and $r=Lj^*$ for the total derived module pullback [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], identified with levelwise $D(j^*)$. Use the relative K-flat derived tensors [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] on $C_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T})$. Let $\eta:1\to re$ and $\varepsilon:er\to1$ be the unit and counit of the derived open adjunction, obtained by deriving the module adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek]. Let $\mu_{A,B}:rA\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_U}rB\to r(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_Z}B)$ be the actual lax monoidal map of the derived module pullback, inverse to its oplax map, induced by the module-object pullback and localization structures, rather than a freely chosen tensor isomorphism.
The unit $\eta_K:K\to reK$ is an isomorphism for every $K\in C_U$. For every $K\in C_U$ and $L\in C_Z$, the canonical open projection component
$$q_{j,K,L}=\varepsilon_{eK\otimes L}\circ e(\mu_{eK,L})\circ e(\eta_K\otimes1_{rL}):e(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_U}rL)\longrightarrow eK\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_Z}L$$
is an isomorphism, naturally in $K,L$. Equivalently it is the adjoint of $K\otimes rL\xrightarrow{\eta_K\otimes1}reK\otimes rL\xrightarrow{\mu_{eK,L}}r(eK\otimes L)$; the symmetric version agrees with the projection map of [def-sfb-adjunction-has-projection-formula]. In particular, for $\Lambda=\underline{\Qlb}$ (the target's condensed $\mathrm{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}\,\ell$) and bounded constructible $K,L$, it is an isomorphism in $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Z,\Lambda)$ with its restricted adjunction [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-adjunction].
